messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding bug reported by a customer: our npm package's exports map is causing their edge worker bundler to pick the CJS entry and it crashes at runtime (fetch auth/retry differences).
jamal: ugh. do we have a repro? which bundler/edge?
maria: Cloudflare Worker using Wrangler, rollup-plugin-node-resolve. Repro steps from customer: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` then runtime throws `TypeError: Redwood is not a function`.
lia: sounds like they pulled the cjs build in an ESM-only runtime. Can we confirm package.json?
maria: their package.json exports currently: ```json
{
  "exports": {
    ".": "./dist/index.cjs.js",
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  },
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.mjs"
}
```
thomas: yep that's the problem — exports pin to the cjs file so modern bundlers/edge runtimes that prefer exports will never see the ESM `module` field.
lia: also saw a types complaint in their build: TS couldn't resolve types because `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts` but that file uses `export =` (CJS style).
jamal: this probably explains the auth/retry mismatch too: the CJS bundle still uses our old retry layer that polyfilled `fetch` with node-fetch + retry wrapper, while the ESM bundle uses native fetch + new retry hook. So surface behavior differs.
maria: customer hit silent auth failures when token refresh tried to use fetch polyfill that wasn't available in their worker.
lia: quick fix idea: make exports conditional. Example we should publish: ```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
jamal: agreed. also update types to an ESM-friendly d.ts (use `export default` and named exports) so TS in edge projects resolves correctly.
thomas: small note — some bundlers (older rollup) still ignore exports and look at `main`. We should keep `main` pointing to cjs for wide compatibility and `module` to mjs. That combo + conditional exports covers most cases.
maria: PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 — includes conditional exports, fixes types, and a changelog entry. Need a patch release (0.11.2).
lia: can we add a smoke test in CI that runs a tiny Cloudflare worker bundling + node rollup to assert import works? would catch regressions.
jamal: yes — add a workflow using wrangler + `esbuild`/`rollup` to bundle sample-app and then run a small node-based runner that executes the bundled output under `miniflare` or `wrangler dev`.
publish-bot: build 0.11.2-rc.1 published to npm under `next` tag.
thomas: plan for rollout: 1) merge PR, 2) publish patch to `latest`, 3) ping customers who filed issues and offer `next` rc for quick test.
maria: action items — @jamal to update CI smoke tests, @lia to fix typings, @thomas to coordinate publish. I'll notify support and add to onboarding checklist to test sample-apps with edge bundlers.
jamal: noted, will put a short repro script in the sample-apps repo and wire the workflow.
lia: pushed a small typing change to the PR that replaces `export =` with explicit ESM exports (keeps CJS compatibility via `declare const Redwood: ...; export default Redwood;`).
maria: thanks. also adding a small troubleshooting note in docs: "If your runtime picks the wrong entry, check `exports` and ensure your bundler supports conditional exports; as workaround import explicit path `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference/dist/index.mjs'`"
thomas: might be worth a temporary recovery path on our side — add a runtime guard that detects `globalThis.fetch` availability and falls back gracefully instead of throwing.
maria: agreed, will add a tiny guard in runtime. OK closing the loop after PR merges. :thumbsup:
